solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slight about railway enthusiast

parts.note: RE is Latin for 'concerning', a standard crossword 'about'
a buff is a keen fan, as in a train buff

explanation.surface: A trainspotter is being looked down on, or is a little-known hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective in the surface but is the verb (or noun) meaning snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or cold-shoulder them, which is exactly what a curt refusal does.

clue.text: On trial, a criminal who's not lost it

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for someone sane; the answer is the adjective describing them

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A defendant in the dock who is still perfectly sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost it' is slang for having gone mad, so someone who has not lost it is still sane.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sane and level-headed, still in control of their mind, is described as reasonable or sensible.

clue.text: Impudence from defender about cap

parts.note: in football or rugby a back is a defending player
C stands for circa, Latin for 'about'
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A footballer gives cheek about being picked, or not picked, for the national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' suggests an international appearance, but it is just headgear here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky, insolent replies to a superior are a form of rudeness or impertinence.

clue.text: Kidney bean providing half-day merriment, somewhat

indicators.note: only half of the word is wanted, so the back half is dropped

parts.note: a day of the week; its first three letters are kept

indicators.note: somewhat means only to a degree, so just part of the word is kept

parts.note: jollity is merriment; only its opening is kept

explanation.surface: A bean that brings a little fun to a half-holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Frijol is the Spanish word for a bean, familiar from refried beans (frijoles); the day must be Friday, chosen to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Mexican and Spanish cooking the word names the common bean, including the kidney-shaped variety.

clue.text: OK turning west, pulled along and grovelled

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way

parts.note: taken as written
W is the compass abbreviation for west
a towed vehicle is pulled along

explanation.surface: A driver heading west accepts a tow and is humbly grateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK' looks like approval but is just two letters to flip.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowtowing, from a Chinese custom of kneeling and touching the head to the ground, means abasing oneself obsequiously.

clue.text: Call from middle of foyer by unknown

indicators.note: the centre of the word is kept and its ends discarded

parts.note: the inner letters of the entrance hall word
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: Someone calls out from the middle of a theatre lobby to a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cry of a town crier or court officer demanding silence and attention before an announcement.

clue.text: Honest girl in time gets very nearly packed

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another
very nearly means just short of complete, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a girl's name
a packed venue is full; its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A girl turns up on time to find the place almost packed out.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name is fitting: ruth is also an old word for pity, and 'truth' sits inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tells no lies and is sincere in speech is straightforward and honest.

clue.text: Humorist's success following current trends

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
a hit is a success, like a hit record

explanation.surface: A comedian's popularity comes from staying topical.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has', joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase describes someone fashionable and up to date with the latest styles and ideas.

clue.text: US car on motorway is a bumper car

parts.note: Dodge is an American car make
M marks British motorways, as in the M1

explanation.surface: An American car on a British motorway is treated like a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the motorway after the car in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairground cars that drivers steer into one another in an enclosed rink are called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Warning of poison, given aurally

indicators.note: something given to the ear is heard rather than read

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: An alert about poison is spoken out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: A tocsin is an alarm bell or signal; the word sounds exactly like the poison.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an alarm bell rung as a signal of danger, hence any alarm or alert.

clue.text: Rather embarrassed about having paid back

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: embarrassed people go red
rather and quite both mean fairly

explanation.surface: Someone feels sheepish about having repaid a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather' looks like a modifier of 'embarrassed', but it is the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to return or repay, as with requited love or a favour returned.

clue.text: Non-payment on new flat due

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are remade in a different order

parts.note: these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Rent goes unpaid on a newly let apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about rent arrears, which makes 'Non-payment' hide in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Failure to meet a loan or debt obligation is called this in finance.

clue.text: Quick appraisal as soon as it is finished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a brief look over something

definitions.text: as soon as it is finished
definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as two words, at the moment it ends

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is a conjunction phrase meaning 'when it has ended'; hyphenated it is a cursory inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something a quick glance to judge it is an idiom for a rapid, superficial inspection.

clue.text: Songbird's piercing scream when its tail is twisted

indicators.note: the end of the word is twisted round, so its final pair swaps order

parts.note: a shriek is a shrill scream; its last two letters are its tail

explanation.surface: A bird screeches when its tail feathers are tweaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its tail' is the last two letters of the scream, which swap places. The 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrike, or butcher-bird, is a perching songbird known for impaling prey on thorns.

clue.text: Bird gaining weight during beauty treatment

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece lies within another

parts.note: waxing removes body hair at a beauty salon
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Someone puts on pounds while having a salon treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is slang for a woman in Britain, which fits the salon picture, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The waxwing is a crested songbird whose wing feathers have red tips like sealing wax.

clue.text: Proprietary cleaner is partly open — not right! Wrong!

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a door ajar is slightly open
R is the abbreviation for right; it is removed
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: An exasperated note on a cleaning product that leaves a door slightly open.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross that a teacher puts beside a wrong answer replaces the lost letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a well-known brand of scouring powder and household detergent, so a trademarked cleaning product.

clue.text: Primate and staff drinking most of the water

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece is swallowed by another

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A monkey and its keepers drink nearly all the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' could be an archbishop, which a staff would suit, but here it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaque is an Old World monkey, such as the rhesus or Barbary ape, so a primate.

clue.text: Scheming women with Afghan musket cut in half beheaded mutineers

indicators.note: cutting in half leaves only one of two equal parts

parts.note: a jezail is a long Afghan musket; its first half is kept

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter goes

parts.note: mutineers are rebels; the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Dangerous women and mutineers with old guns meet a bloody end.
explanation.walkthrough: The jezail is an obscure weapon from Afghan wars of the 1800s; only its first three letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jezebel, the wicked biblical queen, gives her name to any shameless or scheming woman.

clue.text: Field-gun with zero damage

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: An artillery piece that does no harm at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' reads as the noun in the surface but works as the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece firing shells at high angles, used by field batteries.

clue.text: Body parts, regularly skinned, play up

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the word

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: play is room to move, like slack in a rope

explanation.surface: Skinned knees and children misbehaving in the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play up' looks like misbehaving, but 'play' is slack or room and 'up' flips it.
explanation.definitionFit: The patellae, the small bones covering the front of the knee joints, are body parts.

clue.text: Cry over case of whisky having a nicotine stain?

parts.note: a yell is a loud cry
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the spirit

explanation.surface: Someone cries out over a whisky crate stained by cigarette smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: tobacco tar stains fingers and walls a brownish hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine stains turn fingers and ceilings a dingy brownish tint, so they are somewhat that colour.

clue.text: Gent's gent!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a men's lavatory, informally
second meaning: a man's name, standing for any man

explanation.walkthrough: The Gents is the British term for a men's toilet; the same slang word is also a common male first name.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses this name for a toilet, and as a typical male name it can stand for any man.

clue.text: Some Eskimo squeals where imams call to prayer

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are a run inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the word break

explanation.surface: Inuit cries are heard where Muslim leaders summon the faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim place of worship is where the imam leads congregational prayers.

clue.text: Some enclave neglected up on lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
some means only a portion, so the letters are a run inside the words

parts.note: the run straddling the two words, read upwards

explanation.surface: An abandoned enclave stands beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Geneva lies between Switzerland and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Geneva, Lac Léman in French, is a large Alpine lake on the Swiss-French border.

clue.text: Brazilian dance from cricket team in Test reversal

indicators.note: the word itself orders that the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an exam is a test
a cricket side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricket side suffers a setback in a Test match and somehow dances.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, which suits the team, but here it is just an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The maxixe is a fast Brazilian dance, sometimes called the Brazilian tango, popular around 1900.

clue.text: Complied with former pupil and watched

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: An ex-student followed instructions and kept a lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With former pupil' tempts a solver to join those words, but 'with' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Following an order or rule, doing what it requires, is to comply with it.

clue.text: Encroaching navvies I suspect

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order

parts.note: these letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the labourers of trespassing.
explanation.walkthrough: Navvies are British manual labourers, originally canal diggers; 'suspect' is an adjective here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that intrudes or spreads into territory not its own is intrusive and encroaching.

clue.text: One of five and four of fifteen in France
Forms a line and hints heading north

parts.note: cues are prompts or hints
north is up on a map

explanation.surface: People line up while pointing out which way is north.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no word signalling sound; the hints must simply be heard as the same word as the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in a line waiting one's turn is what the British call this, and the phrasal verb means joining one.

clue.text: Square Italian meal adult tucked into

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: pizza is a classic Italian dish
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up tucks into a pizza, the square Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating, but it is placing the adult inside the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is an Italian public square or open marketplace in a town.

clue.text: Passing wind, single dad goes back indoors

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way
indoors means inside, so one piece sits within another
to wind is to twist and turn, so the letters are twisted around

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A lone father breaks wind and retreats inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing wind' looks like a single phrase, but the comma-free break falls after 'Passing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that is elapsing is going by or slipping away, which is passing in the temporal sense.

clue.text: Rubble from overturned bed — something of a risk

indicators.note: turned over means upside down, so the word reads the other way

parts.note: taken as written, then flipped

indicators.note: only some of the word is wanted, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: the article is ignored; most of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Rubble from a bed that has tipped over poses a hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something of' asks for part of the word, here all but its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken fragments and scattered remains left after destruction are rubble or wreckage.
